text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Cabinet okays 1.8 billion shekel budget cut.
- Defence Minister Mordechai cuts a deal on defence budget.
- Six Arab Israelis arrested on suspicion of aiding Hamas.
- Jordan's King Hussein donates $200,000 for carpets at Dome of Rock.
- Mutual funds' assets down 18 percent in 1996.
- Carmel Bank approves allocation of 24 percent of shares to controlling shareholder Jaques Beer for 13.1 million shekels. Beer expands Carmel holdings to 58 percent.
- Knesset Finance Committee approves regulations for portfolio managers.
HAARETZ
- Prime Minister Netanyahu: sovereignty for Palestinians will raise similar demand from Arabs of Galilee.
- Cut in government spending only 1.2 billion shekels, 600 million shekels to come from growth in revenues.
- Senior Israeli army official: Palestinian Authority holding Katyushas, other missiles seized from Hamas.
- Slowdown in economy continues; rate of GDP growth only 3 percent.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Protest in coalition, some 20 Knesset members oppose budget cuts. Next battle in Knesset finance committee.
- Palestinian President Arafat orders security equipment from Israeli company.
- Russia to renovate Syrian air force.
MAARIV
- Foreign Minister Levy: government has no social sensitivity. Knesset members threaten to vote against budget.
- Turkish newspaper: Mossad trains Turkish agents to liquidate Kurdish leader.
GLOBES
- Government approves additional 1.8 billion in cuts by majority of 14 to 4.
